root_causes.description: The recommendation service's server-side latency is pinned at the histogram ceiling (p50=p95=p99=max=10000 ms, mean 9958 ms) while emitting no error responses, indicating an injected fixed-latency fault. recommendation is a direct dependency of frontend (recommendation → product-catalog), so its slowdown propagates upstream and drives the frontend request timeouts and error spike.

frontend is the entry point (invoked by load-generator) and absorbed the propagated failure: its server error rate spiked (max 5.33 err/s) and its p99 latency rose to the 10000 ms histogram ceiling, consistent with timeouts on downstream recommendation calls rather than an internal fault (CPU normal, memory normal, 0 restarts).

evidence.observed_value: 0 restarts; cpu mean=0.021 (max 0.149); memory ~510 MB stable
evidence.expected_baseline: 0 restarts; no resource saturation -> rules out pod_crash/cpu_stress/memory_stress on frontend

root_causes.description: product-catalog is the shared transitive dependency (recommendation → product-catalog and frontend → product-catalog) and therefore an alternative origin for the ≥10 s latency observed at both recommendation and frontend; it could not be excluded because its own server latency was not captured before the tool budget was exhausted, though it showed zero server errors.

evidence.expected_baseline: ~0 (no hard failures; error metric cannot confirm or exclude a latency fault)

remediation_steps: Confirm the origin of the ~10 s latency by querying product-catalog server p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name="product-catalog",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[2m])) by (le)) and inspecting its span duration inside the slowest traces.
Inspect slow trace 306997b7c8789890 (and other frontend traces >10 s) to identify which child span (recommendation vs product-catalog) holds the delay, pinning down the injected service.

If recommendation is confirmed: check for an active flagd feature flag (e.g. recommendation latency/cache fault), disable it, then roll/restart the recommendation deployment and verify p99 returns to <100 ms.
Add or tighten client timeouts and circuit breakers on frontend→recommendation and recommendation→product-catalog so a single slow dependency cannot drive frontend error rates.
Monitor frontend error_rate and recommendation p99 for 30 minutes after mitigation to confirm recovery.
